question.problem:
For the functions $p(x)$ and $q(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
p(5)=-2,\,{p}^{′}(5)=3,\,q(5)=1,\,{q}^{′}(5)=-4
$$

If $z(x)=(p(x)+2q(x))(3-p(x)),$ compute ${z}^{′}(5).$

${z}^{′}(5)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The product rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(uv)=u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=p(x)+2q(x)$ and $v=3-p(x).$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={p}^{′}(x)+2{q}^{′}(x)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=-{p}^{′}(x).
$$

Substituting this into the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}(x) & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =(p(x)+2q(x))(-{p}^{′}(x))+(3-p(x))({p}^{′}(x)+2{q}^{′}(x)) \\  & =-{p}^{′}(x)(p(x)+2q(x))+(3-p(x))({p}^{′}(x)+2{q}^{′}(x)).\end{aligned}
$$

At $x=5$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}(5) & =-{p}^{′}(5)(p(5)+2q(5))+(3-p(5))({p}^{′}(5)+2{q}^{′}(5)) \\  & =-(3)(-2+2\cdot 1)+(3-(-2))(3+2\cdot (-4)) \\  & =-3\cdot 0+5\cdot (-5) \\  & =-25.\end{aligned}
$$
